evidence_chain: Fact: L3Harris reported Q1 2026 Missile Solutions revenue of $990 million versus $840 million in Q1 2025, an 18% increase, and operating margin of 12.5% versus 11.4%. Source: https://investors.l3harris.com/news/news-details/2026/L3Harris-Technologies-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx

Fact: L3Harris attributed Q1 2026 Missile Solutions revenue growth to higher production volumes across key missile and munition programs, including programs prioritized by the Department of War's Munitions Acceleration Council, plus space propulsion programs and new program ramps. Source: https://investors.l3harris.com/news/news-details/2026/L3Harris-Technologies-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx

Fact: L3Harris' 2025 annual report states the Aerojet Rocketdyne segment includes missile solutions with propulsion technologies for strategic defense, missile defense, hypersonics and tactical systems, plus space propulsion and power systems; it also reports higher Missile Solutions volume on key missile and munitions programs and new program ramps. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/sites/default/files/2026-04/L3Harris-2025-Annual-Report.pdf

Fact: L3Harris disclosed a Space Technology disposal group involving certain Space Propulsion and Power Systems product lines and space-related assets, with associated goodwill impairment and held-for-sale assets. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/sites/default/files/2026-04/L3Harris-2025-Annual-Report.pdf

Fact: L3Harris broke ground in February 2025 on four new solid rocket motor production facilities at Camden, Arkansas, under a $215.6 million Defense Production Act Title III cooperative agreement intended to increase domestic rocket propulsion manufacturing capacity. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/press-release/2025/02/l3harris-breaks-ground-solid-rocket-motor-factories-future-arkansas

Fact: L3Harris said the Camden expansion includes a 60,000-square-foot facility, a dedicated mixer building, and propellant processing buildings intended to support increased motor production. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/press-release/2025/02/l3harris-breaks-ground-solid-rocket-motor-factories-future-arkansas

Fact: Aerojet Rocketdyne said its $215.6 million DoD cooperative agreement supports higher demand primarily for Javelin, Stinger and GMLRS, and that it was procuring specialized long-lead equipment such as large-capacity mixers and grinders. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/editorial/2024/05/factories-future-aerojet-rocketdyne-completes-key-milestones-expansion

Fact: Aerojet Rocketdyne described site specialization: Camden for medium and large solid rocket motors, Orange County, Virginia for small motors, and Huntsville for inert work such as case-winding and nozzle production. Source: https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/editorial/2024/05/factories-future-aerojet-rocketdyne-completes-key-milestones-expansion

Fact: In early 2026, L3Harris said it created a Missile Solutions business combining capabilities for offensive and defensive missile systems and intended to pursue an IPO of the Missile Solutions business in the second half of 2026. Source: https://investors.l3harris.com/news/news-details/2026/L3Harris-Accelerates-Arsenal-of-Freedom-with-Creation-of-a-New-Missile-Solutions-Company/default.aspx

Inference: The strongest Serenity-style chokepoint signal is not just revenue growth; it is the combination of government-funded capacity expansion, long-lead equipment, energetic-manufacturing permitting, site specialization, and rising production volumes in missile and munition programs.
falsification_plan: Falsify if Missile Solutions / Aerojet backlog, orders or book-to-bill weakens despite visible policy demand for munitions and missile defense.
Falsify if production-rate targets slip because Camden, Huntsville or Orange County expansions fail to pass qualification, staffing, permitting or safety milestones.

Falsify if quarterly Missile Solutions revenue growth decelerates materially while primes and DoD continue to report strong missile demand, implying share loss, bottleneck failure or program execution issues.
Falsify if operating margin remains structurally weak or deteriorates despite higher volume, indicating the node is not capturing chokepoint economics.
Falsify if the Space Technology disposal group, Missile Solutions IPO or other portfolio actions leave LHX with materially less retained missile-propulsion economics than assumed.
Falsify if DoD or prime contractors rapidly shift propulsion content to alternative suppliers, reducing Aerojet Rocketdyne's scarcity value.

Falsify if government budget lines for GMLRS, Javelin, Stinger, PAC-3, THAAD, Standard Missile, Tomahawk, hypersonics or Golden Dome / missile defense materially disappoint versus current expectations.
next_research_tasks: Normalize reporting history: build a bridge from Aerojet Rocketdyne legacy segment to 2026 Missile Solutions, separating Missile Propulsion, Space Propulsion & Power Systems, Advanced Effects and assets held for sale.

Extract the latest Q1 2026 10-Q and earnings call transcript to verify backlog, orders, book-to-bill, EAC adjustments, program commentary and any Missile Solutions IPO details not visible in the press release.

Map program exposure by missile family: GMLRS, Javelin, Stinger, PAC-3, THAAD, Tomahawk, Standard Missile, strategic missiles, hypersonics and interceptors; identify whether L3Harris supplies booster, sustainer, DACS, warhead/fuzing, inert components or other propulsion content.

Track capacity milestones: Camden 60,000-square-foot facility, mixer building, propellant processing buildings, Huntsville AMF-South inert component line, Orange County small-motor transition, hiring, equipment installation, qualification runs and first delivery dates.

Check government-source evidence: DoD contract announcements, DPA Title III updates, Army / Navy / MDA budget justification books, and FMS notifications for missile programs with Aerojet propulsion content.

Compare alternative suppliers and dual-sourcing: Northrop Grumman, Anduril, Ursa Major, X-Bow and other solid rocket motor entrants; determine where they compete versus where Aerojet remains embedded.

Build a quarterly monitoring table: Missile Solutions revenue, operating income, margin, orders, backlog, book-to-bill, capex, LHX NeXt savings, EAC adjustments, late deliveries and quality commentary.
Stress-test political demand: separate base-budget programs from supplemental funding, Ukraine replenishment, Indo-Pacific posture, missile-defense / Golden Dome initiatives, and allied FMS demand.
risks: Portfolio-purity risk: Space Technology disposal and the creation / potential IPO of Missile Solutions may change LHX's retained exposure to missile propulsion; the thesis must be updated when transaction terms, retained stake, governance and segment reporting become clearer.

Execution risk: Announced capacity does not equal qualified output. Facilities, mixers, grinders, propellant processing buildings, inert component lines and automation must translate into accepted motor deliveries.

Margin risk: Higher volume may not improve profitability if fixed-price exposure, unfavorable EAC adjustments, supplier inflation, labor shortages, quality escapes or integration costs absorb the benefit.
Customer concentration and program risk: Demand is tied to U.S. government and allied defense budgets, program timing, contract awards and prime contractor schedules.

Political risk: Defense priorities can shift after elections, budget negotiations, continuing resolutions, export approvals, Ukraine / Indo-Pacific policy changes or missile-defense architecture changes.
Competition / substitution risk: DoD may fund alternative solid rocket motor suppliers or dual-source programs to reduce dependence on legacy suppliers.
Regulatory and environmental risk: Energetic manufacturing requires safety, environmental and permitting compliance; NEPA or local permitting delays could slow capacity additions.
Accounting and comparability risk: L3Harris has changed business structure and reporting segments, so historical Aerojet Rocketdyne comparisons may be misleading unless recast consistently.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme: Politics -> defense budgets, wartime replenishment, allied FMS, missile-defense policy, industrial-base policy. Demand nodes: Javelin, Stinger, GMLRS, PAC-3, THAAD, Tomahawk, Standard Missile, hypersonics, strategic missiles and interceptors. Prime/integrator layer: Lockheed Martin, RTX/Raytheon, Boeing, Northrop Grumman and government program offices. Chokepoint layer: propulsion systems, solid rocket motors, propellant mixing/casting, motor cases, nozzles, aft closures, exit cones, inert components, energetic manufacturing permits, qualification and acceptance testing. L3Harris / Aerojet Rocketdyne position: upstream propulsion supplier and manufacturing-capacity node across Camden, Huntsville, Orange County and other facilities. Bottleneck attributes: hazardous energetic manufacturing, specialized equipment such as large-capacity mixers and grinders, long permitting and NEPA processes, customer qualification, limited qualified supplier base, and need for government-funded capacity expansion.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：L3Harris 的关键研究价值不在传统国防电子叙事，而在 Aerojet Rocketdyne / Missile Solutions 所代表的导弹推进、固体火箭发动机和相关弹药推进产能。若美国及盟友继续推动弹药库存补充、导弹防御、精确火力、高超音速和拦截弹项目扩产，推进剂处理、固体火箭发动机制造、质量认证、长周期设备和客户验收节奏可能成为上游约束。事实层面，L3Harris 2026 年一季度按新分部披露 Missile Solutions 收入 9.90 亿美元，同比增长 18%，经营利润率 12.5%；公司称增长来自重点导弹和弹药项目、更高产量、空间推进项目和新项目爬坡。需要注意：用户缓存中提到的“Q1 2026 Aerojet Rocketdyne 收入约 7.12 亿美元、2026 指引约 28 亿美元”可能来自旧口径或中间材料；本轮联网核验到的最新官方一季报采用 Missile Solutions 新分部口径，因此后续跟踪应统一口径，避免把 Aerojet Rocketdyne、Missile Solutions、Space Propulsion & Power Systems 和待剥离 Space Technology 混在一起。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: L3Harris' most relevant politics-linked chokepoint exposure is not generic defense electronics, but Aerojet Rocketdyne / Missile Solutions: missile propulsion, solid rocket motors, and related munitions propulsion capacity. If U.S. and allied policy continues to prioritize munitions replenishment, missile defense, precision fires, hypersonics, and interceptors, then propellant processing, solid-rocket-motor manufacturing, qualification throughput, long-lead equipment, and customer acceptance rates may become binding upstream constraints. As a verified fact, L3Harris' Q1 2026 release under the new segment structure reported Missile Solutions revenue of $990 million, up 18%, with 12.5% operating margin; management attributed growth to higher production volumes across key missile and munition programs, space propulsion programs, and new program ramps. Caveat: the cached brief's Q1 2026 Aerojet Rocketdyne revenue of about $712 million and 2026 outlook of about $2.8 billion may reflect an older or different reporting perimeter; the latest official Q1 2026 release uses Missile Solutions, so future tracking must keep Aerojet Rocketdyne, Missile Solutions, Space Propulsion & Power Systems, and the Space Technology disposal group analytically separate.
deep_reports.title_cn: L3Harris / Aerojet Rocketdyne：美国导弹推进与固体火箭发动机扩产链条中的上游卡点
deep_reports.title_en: L3Harris / Aerojet Rocketdyne: Upstream Missile-Propulsion Chokepoint in the U.S. Defense-Industrial-Base Rebuild

evidence_chain: Fact: BWXT reported that it ended 2025 with backlog of about $7.3 billion, up 50% year over year, driven by large multi-year naval propulsion, special materials, and commercial nuclear power awards. Source: https://investors.bwxt.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bwx-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025

Fact: BWXT reported Q1 2026 backlog by segment of approximately $6.93 billion in Government Operations and $1.72 billion in Commercial Operations, totaling about $8.65 billion. Source: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260504964337/en/BWX-Technologies-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results

Fact: In Q1 2026, BWXT said Government Operations revenue growth was driven by higher special materials processing revenue and naval reactors growth, partly offset by lower microreactor volumes. Source: https://investors.bwxt.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bwx-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-results/

Fact: BWXT announced more than $1.4 billion of Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program contracts in May 2026, including a $1.285 billion fiscal-2026 base contract for long-lead material procurement and a $165 million contract for long-lead reactor-system components and Ford-class carrier manufacturing work. Source: https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/bwxt-announces-14-billion-contracts-naval-nuclear-propulsion-program-2026-05-07

Fact: BWXT stated that manufacturing work under the $165 million award will occur at Barberton, Ohio, and Mount Vernon, Indiana facilities. Source: https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/bwxt-announces-14-billion-contracts-naval-nuclear-propulsion-program-2026-05-07
Inference: The size and government-weighted composition of backlog suggest BWXT is exposed to durable U.S. political priorities around nuclear-powered sea control and nuclear deterrence.

Inference: The chokepoint is likely more institutional and regulatory than purely technological: qualification, safety culture, classified program access, and production history may matter more than near-term design novelty.

Hypothesis: If submarine and carrier nuclear-propulsion funding remains politically protected, BWXT could have a multi-year demand runway, but the realized equity story depends on execution quality, not just awards.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if Government Operations backlog declines materially for multiple quarters or book-to-bill weakens without a clear timing explanation.
Downgrade the thesis if naval nuclear propulsion revenue grows but segment margins compress persistently, implying the chokepoint is not translating into economic control.
Downgrade the thesis if Columbia-class, Virginia-class, or Ford-class procurement schedules are materially delayed, reduced, or reprioritized.
Downgrade the thesis if BWXT discloses a significant nuclear quality, safety, regulatory, cybersecurity, or security-clearance issue.
Downgrade the thesis if hiring, retention, capex, or supply-chain constraints prevent conversion of backlog into revenue.
Downgrade the thesis if commercial nuclear initiatives absorb capital and management attention without improving returns or strategic control.

Upgrade evidence quality only after verifying contract-level content, margin profile, funded versus unfunded backlog, and facility-level capacity constraints through filings, budget documents, and contract databases.
next_research_tasks: Parse BWXT 2025 Form 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q for funded versus unfunded backlog, remaining performance obligations, segment margins, working capital, capex, and risk-factor language.
Build a contract timeline for 2024-2026 Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program awards, separating long-lead material, reactor components, fuel, steam generators, and special-materials work.
Map BWXT facilities by role: Lynchburg, Barberton, Mount Vernon, Erwin, Cambridge/Ontario and acquired assets; identify which facilities are true bottlenecks.
Check U.S. Navy FY2026 and FY2027 budget documents for Columbia-class, Virginia-class, Ford-class, submarine industrial base, and naval reactors funding lines.
Compare BWXT’s Government Operations margin trend versus backlog growth to test whether political demand is economically attractive or merely volume-heavy.
Review labor-market disclosures, hiring plans, union/retention issues, and nuclear-skilled workforce constraints.
Separate defense-nuclear thesis from commercial nuclear optionality: evaluate whether SMR, nuclear medicine, Canadian nuclear services, and Kinectrics improve or dilute the core chokepoint thesis.
Create a falsification dashboard tracking quarterly Government Operations backlog, revenue, operating income, book-to-bill, capex, free cash flow, and disclosed program delays.
risks: Execution risk: large regulated nuclear programs can encounter schedule delays, cost overruns, quality escapes, or rework.
Labor bottleneck risk: specialized nuclear manufacturing depends on scarce engineers, welders, machinists, safety personnel, and cleared workers.
Margin conversion risk: backlog growth may not be margin-accretive if newer special-materials projects, mix, inflation, labor costs, or fixed-price exposure pressure profitability.

Budget and appropriations risk: U.S. defense and nuclear programs are politically important but still exposed to continuing resolutions, funding delays, procurement changes, debt-ceiling politics, and shifting acquisition priorities.
Compliance and safety risk: nuclear manufacturing has low tolerance for regulatory, safety, security, or quality failures; any major issue could disrupt production and reputation.
Capital intensity risk: capacity expansion, facility modernization, acquisitions, and working capital may consume cash before revenue and profit fully materialize.
Commercial distraction risk: commercial nuclear, SMR components, nuclear medicine, and acquisitions may add growth optionality but could dilute focus or introduce integration risk.
Market-pricing risk: a strong political/nuclear narrative may already be reflected in valuation; this report does not assess fair value or provide a price target.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Theme: Politics / defense industrial base / nuclear deterrence. Demand layer: U.S. Navy nuclear-powered submarines and aircraft carriers; nuclear deterrence; national-security nuclear materials; commercial nuclear revival as secondary adjacency. System layer: naval nuclear propulsion systems, reactor components, long-lead material procurement, fuel, steam generators, and special-materials processing. Chokepoint node: regulated nuclear manufacturing requiring security clearance, nuclear safety culture, process qualification, specialized labor, and government program integration. Public-market mapping: BWXT is the primary listed pure-play exposure in this map; it should be compared with large primes and shipbuilders, but its distinctive research angle is upstream nuclear-manufacturing scarcity rather than platform assembly.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：BWXT 不是普通军工供应商，而是美国海军核推进、特种核材料、核燃料和核部件制造中的稀缺受监管节点。其卡点来自核安全资质、长期客户关系、保密要求、复杂工艺控制、监管壁垒和长周期认证。政治需求端由 Columbia 级战略核潜艇、Virginia 级攻击核潜艇、Ford 级航母、核威慑现代化和潜艇工业基础扩张共同驱动。关键研究问题不是需求是否存在，而是积压订单能否在不牺牲利润率、现金流和执行质量的情况下转化为收入。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: BWXT is less a generic defense contractor and more a scarce regulated-production node in U.S. naval nuclear propulsion, special nuclear materials, nuclear fuel, and nuclear components. Its chokepoint characteristics come from nuclear qualification, long-standing customer relationships, classified/security requirements, process-control difficulty, regulatory barriers, and long-cycle validation. Political demand is tied to Columbia-class SSBNs, Virginia-class SSNs, Ford-class carriers, nuclear-deterrence modernization, and submarine-industrial-base expansion. The key research question is not whether demand exists, but whether backlog converts into revenue without margin, cash-flow, workforce, or compliance slippage.
deep_reports.title_cn: BWXT：美国海军核推进与受监管核制造的政治型卡点
deep_reports.title_en: BWXT: A Political Chokepoint in U.S. Naval Nuclear Propulsion and Regulated Nuclear Manufacturing

evidence_chain: [Fact] HII's FY2025 Form 10-K reported total backlog of approximately $53.1 billion as of December 31, 2025, versus $48.7 billion as of December 31, 2024. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001501585/000150158526000006/hii-20251231.htm

[Fact] HII's FY2025 Form 10-K said it expected approximately 21% of the $53.1 billion year-end 2025 backlog to convert into sales during 2026. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001501585/000150158526000006/hii-20251231.htm

[Fact] HII's Q1 2026 earnings release reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.1 billion, up 13.4% year over year, and new awards of $4.0 billion, bringing total backlog to $54.0 billion as of March 31, 2026. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1501585/000150158526000027/hii2026q1earningsrelease.htm

[Fact] HII's FY2025 results release said 2025 revenue increased to $12.5 billion and highlighted 2025 milestones including delivery of Virginia-class submarine Massachusetts and guided missile destroyer Ted Stevens. Source: https://www.hii.com/news/hii-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results/

[Fact] HII described itself in its FY2025 filing as America's largest shipbuilder, with Newport News and Ingalls segments building more ships in more ship classes than any other U.S. naval shipbuilder. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1501585/000150158526000006/hii-20251231.htm

[Fact] HII's FY2025 filing disclosed that Newport News sales and service revenues increased in 2025 primarily from higher volumes in submarines and aircraft carriers, and that Ingalls sales and service revenues also increased year over year. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001501585/000150158526000016/hii_2025arfinal.pdf

[Fact] HII disclosed performance challenges at Newport News in aircraft carrier construction and the Virginia-class submarine program, which directly supports the margin-risk side of the thesis. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001501585/000150158526000006/hii-20251231.htm

[Inference] The evidence supports a real bottleneck thesis because demand is visible through backlog and naval programs, while supply expansion is constrained by yard infrastructure, skilled labor, supplier qualification, and nuclear-program experience.

[Inference] The evidence does not yet prove value capture. High backlog can coexist with poor margins if schedule delays, labor inefficiency, late material, or contract structures transfer cost inflation to HII rather than the customer.
falsification_plan: Backlog remains near record levels, but annual or quarterly backlog conversion slows materially versus management expectations.
Newport News or Ingalls revenue grows while segment operating margin deteriorates, indicating cost leakage rather than value capture.
Virginia-class, Columbia-class, Ford-class, DDG-51, or amphibious-ship milestones slip repeatedly across multiple reporting periods.
Management discloses persistent late material, supplier shortages, rework, absenteeism, retention problems, or inability to scale skilled labor.
Contract modifications fail to offset wage inflation, supplier inflation, or schedule disruption.
Free cash flow guidance or reported free cash flow weakens despite strong awards and backlog.
Congress, the Navy, or DoD redirects procurement emphasis away from large naval platforms where HII has strongest exposure.
A competitor or government-led distributed shipbuilding model reduces HII's practical bottleneck control faster than expected.
next_research_tasks: Pull the full FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q/8-K tables; extract backlog by segment, awards by segment, revenue by segment, operating income, operating margin, and free cash flow.

Create a program tracker for Virginia-class, Columbia-class, Ford-class, carrier RCOH, DDG-51, amphibious ships, and small surface combatants; track award dates, delivery milestones, delays, and contract modifications.
Verify yard-level throughput claims at Newport News and Ingalls using company filings, Navy budget documents, GAO shipbuilding reports, and congressional testimony.
Build a labor dashboard: headcount, apprentice pipeline, hiring targets, attrition, absenteeism, union issues, training capacity, and master shipbuilder retention.
Map the upstream supplier bottlenecks: nuclear components, castings/forgings, propulsion, electrical systems, valves, pumps, combat systems, and specialized materials.
Compare HII with General Dynamics Electric Boat/Bath Iron Works exposure inside GD to understand relative chokepoint purity and program overlap.
Review Navy FY2027 budget request, shipbuilding plan, submarine industrial-base funding, and AUKUS-related appropriations when available.
Check whether revenue growth is being accompanied by sustainable segment margin and cash conversion; do not treat backlog alone as sufficient confirmation.
Search GAO, CRS, Navy, and DoD Inspector General materials for independent evidence of shipbuilding delays, cost overruns, and industrial-base constraints.
Monitor HII management commentary on contract type, cost recovery, supplier health, hiring, distributed shipbuilding, and capital expenditure intensity.
risks: [Execution risk] Ship delivery schedules may slip even while backlog remains high, weakening the link between policy demand and revenue realization.
[Margin risk] Labor inefficiency, rework, supplier delays, inflation, or unfavorable fixed-price exposure could cause the bottleneck to capture cost rather than profit.
[Labor risk] Skilled-trade hiring, training, retention, absenteeism, retirement, and productivity are central to throughput; failure here would directly challenge the thesis.
[Supply-chain risk] Nuclear-qualified components, castings, forgings, propulsion-related inputs, combat systems, and other specialized parts can delay yard execution.

[Budget risk] U.S. Navy procurement priorities, continuing resolutions, shipbuilding appropriations, program cancellations, or changes in platform mix could shift demand away from HII's strongest exposures.
[Program concentration risk] HII depends heavily on U.S. government and Navy programs; this creates durable demand but also customer concentration, political oversight, and contract-negotiation risk.
[Cash-flow risk] Long-cycle programs can create working-capital pressure even when accounting revenue and backlog look healthy.

[Market-pricing risk] If the market already prices HII as a scarce naval-industrial-base asset, positive policy news may have limited incremental effect unless margins, cash flow, and delivery cadence improve.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand layer: U.S. Navy, Department of Defense, Congress, shipbuilding appropriations, AUKUS and allied maritime posture. Platform layer: Virginia-class attack submarines, Columbia-class ballistic-missile submarine modules, Ford-class aircraft carriers, carrier refueling and complex overhaul, DDG-51 destroyers, amphibious ships, and naval modernization. System-integrator/chokepoint layer: HII Newport News and Ingalls shipyards; nuclear-capable shipbuilding know-how; dry docks; construction halls; program management; qualified skilled trades; supplier coordination. Upstream layer: steel, castings, forgings, nuclear components, propulsion systems, combat systems, electrical systems, valves, pumps, cabling, and thousands of qualified defense suppliers. Public-market mapping: HII is the listed prime yard exposure; General Dynamics Electric Boat is the main submarine peer inside GD; many suppliers are private or embedded in broader defense companies.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: HII 是美国政治与国防预算主题下最纯的海军造船工业基础上市暴露之一。它的卡点不是某个单一零部件，而是综合船厂系统：核潜艇与航母经验、船坞、熟练工、供应商网络、核项目认证、长周期建造管理和海军项目执行能力。若美国继续强调潜艇、航母、驱逐舰、两栖舰、AUKUS 和盟友海上能力，HII 的稀缺性会被持续验证。但这个 thesis 的关键不在于 backlog 本身，而在于 backlog 能否按期、按成本、带利润地转化为收入和现金流。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis] HII is one of the purest listed exposures to the U.S. naval shipbuilding industrial base within the politics and defense-budget theme. The chokepoint is not a single component; it is the integrated shipyard system: nuclear-submarine and carrier know-how, dry docks, skilled trades, qualified suppliers, nuclear program credentials, long-cycle build management, and Navy program execution. If U.S. policy continues to prioritize submarines, carriers, destroyers, amphibious ships, AUKUS, and allied maritime capacity, HII's scarcity value should remain strategically important. The key test, however, is not backlog alone; it is whether backlog converts into revenue, margin, and cash flow without schedule slippage or cost leakage.
deep_reports.title_cn: HII：美国海军造船工业基础的稀缺产能卡点
deep_reports.title_en: HII: Scarce U.S. Naval Shipbuilding Capacity as a Defense-Industrial Chokepoint

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
